name: @gaterook/design-kit
description: GateRook design system: tokens (light, dark, high contrast), SCSS components, elements, app page references and AI consumption rules. Source of truth for every screen of the desktop app.

icons.angular: lucide-angular (a release that bundles every icon name used; verify with npm run icons)

components.name: gw-logo
components.purpose: Product lockup: the mark (assets/logo-mark.svg, never redrawn) plus the product name set in the UI font.
components.a11y: The link carries the accessible name (aria-label); the mark img has alt="".

components.name: gw-icon / gw-icon-tile / gw-spinner
components.purpose: Lucide icon wrapper (pinned in vendor/lucide), tinted icon tile with tones, in-place spinner.
variants: icon: xs sm md lg xl 2xl
tile: sm lg + tones brand success warning danger info neutral dev stage prod
components.a11y: Icons are aria-hidden (kit.js sets it); meaning lives in adjacent text. Spinner pulses instead of rotating under reduced motion.

components.name: gw-btn / gw-btn-group
components.purpose: The single button primitive. Primary = the one main action of a view; approve = only the approval decision; danger = confirming an irreversible action; danger-ghost = its trigger.
subparts: __pressed (face shown while aria-pressed=true; Live: a gw-status--live dot)
__unpressed (face shown while aria-pressed is not true; Live: the radio icon)
states: :disabled (nothing to explain) / aria-disabled=true + aria-describedby (unavailable with a reason; kit.js blocks it)
aria-busy + gw-spinner
aria-pressed=true (toggle, data-gw-pressed flips it): brand tone AND a 2px brand bar along the bottom edge (shape, not only colour); only the matching __pressed / __unpressed face shows
components.a11y: Native <button type> or <a href>; icon-only needs aria-label naming the object.

components.name: gw-card / gw-stack
components.purpose: The one container: header (title, description, actions), body, footer. gw-stack spaces stacked cards.
components.a11y: section[aria-labelledby] → the title heading. Interactive cards use one stretched link; selected pairs with aria-current/aria-checked.

components.name: gw-shell
components.purpose: Window frame of every app page: a CSS grid with the titlebar across the top, the sidebar on the left and main on the right. The window never scrolls as a whole: the shell is 100vh/100dvh, capped by max-height: 100% of a sized parent, and the sidebar body and main each scroll on their own. Copy it verbatim from pages/_shell.html.
variants: (no sidebar) main spans the full width: onboarding, core status screen
states: [data-collapsed] sidebar shrinks to --gw-layout-sidebar-collapsed (kit.js data-gw-sidebar-toggle, persisted in localStorage)
below md: collapsed automatically, toggle hidden
components.a11y: A skip link (gw-skip-link) before the shell targets main#main[tabindex=-1]; the programmatic focus target gets no ring. Landmarks appear once each, in order: header (titlebar) → nav[aria-label=Main] → main. The grid has exactly three children: app-wide banners (gw-alert--banner) go first inside __main. The sidebar width change animates only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

components.name: gw-titlebar
components.purpose: Electron frameless titlebar (bg canvas, subtle bottom rule, --gw-layout-titlebar-height): current section name, a drag spacer and actions (search with ⌘K, approvals bell with an attention counter, appearance popover). The whole bar is a drag region; links, buttons, inputs, labels, [tabindex], menus and popovers inside opt out (no-drag) automatically.
variants: Windows/Linux: end padding from env(titlebar-area-x/width); the fallbacks cancel out without Window Controls Overlay
states: a gw-counter inside an icon button in __actions is pinned as a corner badge ringed in the canvas colour
components.a11y:
The
is the banner landmark. Icon buttons carry aria-label ("Approvals, 3 waiting" with an aria-hidden counter; "Appearance"). The Search button's name starts with its visible text ("Search and commands") and its ⌘K kbd is aria-hidden. Overlays at the window edge use gw-menu--right / gw-popover--right. Popover titles are

, not headings, because they precede the page h1.

components.name: gw-sidebar
components.purpose: Navigation column (bg.sidebar, end border): logo and collapse toggle, the scrolling nav, and a footer that always shows the local core and the tunnel (gw-status, static) plus the mono address and version line.
states: collapsed (.gw-shell[data-collapsed] or below md): the header stacks; the logo name, footer status labels and __meta become sr-only; status dots stay; __toggle is hidden below md
components.a11y: A plain <div>, not <aside>, because primary navigation is not complementary. The toggle is a button with data-gw-sidebar-toggle, aria-controls pointing at the sidebar id and aria-expanded kept in sync by kit.js. While expanded, the footer uses gw-status with words, never a dot alone. It is never gw-status--live: an endless pulse on every screen fails WCAG 2.2.2.

components.name: gw-nav
components.purpose: The app's information architecture (BLUEPRINT §2): Overview and Approvals (counter), then the Resources, Access and Observe groups, with Settings pinned at the bottom. Items are 32px rows: a 16px icon, a label and muted text.
variants: __group--end (pinned to the bottom behind a hairline)
states: aria-current="page": bg.selected, primary text, semibold, a 2px brand-fg bar at the inline start (drawn as a border, so it survives forced colours) and a brand-fg icon
:hover wash + primary text
:active wash
:focus-visible inset ring

collapsed: label and group labels sr-only, hairlines between groups. Counter becomes an 8px border-drawn dot on the icon corner: --attention warning, plain neutral, --muted sr-only. The label flies out beside the icon on :hover AND :focus-visible (tooltip look, hoverable through a bridge; anchor positioning where anchor-scope is supported, fixed static-position fallback)
components.a11y:
Items are with exactly one aria-current="page" per page. Labelled groups use role="group" + aria-labelledby pointing at the visible __group-label (a

, not a heading). Counters carry sr-only words: , 3 waiting. Collapsed links keep their accessible name. The

must be identical on every page (checked); demos omit data-gw-nav.

components.name: gw-page
components.purpose: The content container inside gw-shell__main and the only way to cap a width. Gutters are --gw-layout-page-gutter (16px below sm), content max is --gw-layout-content-max, and children stack 32px apart.
variants: --full (no cap, min-height 100%; a direct gw-split child fills the remaining height of main)
states: below md: inside --full, a gw-split stops filling and the page scrolls
components.a11y: Holds exactly one gw-page-header, which carries the page h1. Never set max-width or margin: 0 auto on page content.

components.name: gw-page-header
components.purpose: Top of every page: an optional breadcrumb, then a title row (heading on the left with the h1, description and meta; actions on the right), then an optional tabs slot.
states: narrow: the heading keeps at least 18rem; actions drop under it and wrap (they shrink instead of overflowing)
long literal titles break (overflow-wrap: anywhere)
components.a11y: __title is the page's only h1. Meta that names an environment uses gw-env with sr-only 'environment' before it. Tabs in __tabs follow gw-tabs (role=tablist). Primary action last; at most one --primary.

components.name: gw-breadcrumb
components.purpose: Path to a nested page (endpoint-detail, connection-new): nav[aria-label=Breadcrumb] > ol > li, with a chevron-right gw-icon before every item after the first.
states: current item: aria-current="page" (a <span>, or a link to the page itself), secondary text, medium weight, truncates
links: muted, :hover primary + underline, :focus-visible ring
components.a11y: The separator icon is decorative (kit.js sets aria-hidden). Links keep a 24px target height. Literal names (slugs, connection names) use gw-mono.

components.name: gw-section
components.purpose: A titled block of a page without a card: __header (h2 title and one-line description on the left, actions on the right) followed by the content, 12px apart. Use a card instead when the block needs its own surface or footer.
states: below sm: the actions drop under the title and description
components.a11y: <section aria-labelledby> pointing at the __title (h2 on a page, one level below the surrounding heading elsewhere).

components.name: gw-toolbar
components.purpose: Row of filters and actions above a table or list. __start holds search and filters and wraps; __end holds actions, stays at the end and wraps onto its own line when space runs out.
variants: --sticky (pinned to the top of the scrolling main with a canvas fill; only for toolbars sitting on the page canvas)
components.a11y: Controls inside are kit controls with visible labels or aria-labels; a result count is plain text next to the filters. Group related controls with gw-divider--vertical (aria-hidden).

components.name: gw-split
components.purpose: Master-detail layout (Approvals, Playground): __list and __detail, each scrolling on its own once the split has a height. Inside gw-page--full it takes the rest of main; elsewhere set --gw-split-height.
states: below lg (a window under 1280px, where the list would get under ~320px): the panels stack, the height is dropped and the page scrolls (also inside gw-page--full)
components.a11y: Panels keep 4px of inner room so focus rings are not clipped. A panel with nothing focusable inside gets tabindex="0" + role="region" + aria-label so the keyboard can scroll it. The current list item carries aria-current or aria-selected plus a second cue.

components.name: gw-grid
components.purpose: Responsive grid of cards or stat tiles with a 16px gap. It works on <div>, <ul> and <dl>.
variants: --auto (auto-fill, minimum column --gw-grid-min = 280px, override per use; use it inside narrow panels)
components.a11y: Pure layout. DOM order is reading order; never reorder visually.

components.name: gw-divider
components.purpose: Hairline (border.default) between groups of content that share a surface. Between cards, use the gap instead.
variants: --vertical (20px tall, between inline items such as meta, toolbar groups and counts)
components.a11y: Horizontal: <hr class="gw-divider"> (role separator). Vertical: a <span> with aria-hidden="true", or role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" when the split is meaningful.

components.name: gw-kbd
components.purpose: A key the user presses, in running text, help, menus and the command palette: one <kbd> per key, adjacent keys 2px apart, caption-size mono on surface with a strong border and a 2px bottom edge.
components.a11y: Keys are written as text (Esc, Enter, Shift, ⌘). Arrow and return keys are Lucide icons (arrow-up, arrow-down, corner-down-left) plus sr-only text. A decorative hint next to a labelled control is aria-hidden. Inside a button use gw-btn__kbd; inside gw-search use gw-search__kbd.

components.name: gw-avatar
components.purpose: A person (approver, user in server mode): two uppercase initials on a neutral circle, or a photo.
states: with __img: surface fill, the image covers the circle
components.a11y: Next to a visible name: aria-hidden="true" (and alt="" on __img). Standing alone: role="img" + aria-label with the full name (or a meaningful alt on __img). The 1px border keeps the shape in forced colours.

components.name: gw-client-mark
components.purpose: Neutral monogram tile of an MCP client (rounded square, so it never reads like a person or an env marker). It is never a vendor logo: official marks come only from vendor press kits after sign-off. Each app keeps one tile everywhere: client cards, endpoint AI apps, Activity rows.
variants: --generic (any other client: dashed outline, initials or an app-window icon)
components.a11y: Decorative next to a visible name (aria-hidden="true"); alone, role="img" + aria-label with the full client name. The tone is an identity hue only: status, warning, danger and prod tones are never used, and connection state is a gw-status beside the tile. Each tile has a 1px border for forced colours; text pairs are verified tone fg on tone subtle, on-solid on solid, and inverse.

components.name: gw-badge / gw-counter
components.purpose: Badge: a 20px status pill in sentence case with an optional leading icon. It names the decision on a call, a token's lifetime, a connector's kind or an MCP annotation, using the BLUEPRINT §7 vocabulary. Counter: a bare 18px number beside a nav item, tab or button; amber (--attention) means a human is waiting.
variants: gw-badge--solid (env tones keep the tint and get a solid edge)
subparts: gw-badge__icon (12px; any direct .gw-icon child is sized the same)
states: display only: no interactive states
never wraps or truncates: keep the words short
components.a11y: Words are always present; the icon is an aria-hidden second cue. Tone fg on tone subtle and on-solid on solid are verified 4.5:1 in all four modes. A counter needs sr-only context ('3 waiting') or a control name that says what is counted. The badge border and the counter's transparent border keep the shape in forced colors.

components.name: gw-status
components.purpose: Dot plus label for the health of a connection, the core, the tunnel or a client (BLUEPRINT §7 health vocabulary). The words state the state; the dot is the second cue.
subparts: gw-status__dot (8px tone-fg dot with a 1px tone-border outline ring, in a 12px slot)
states: --live: the ring pulses inside gw-motion; under reduced motion it is a static ring; one per view
--checking: covers checking and starting; a spinner replaces the dot (a __dot left in the markup is hidden), and the label does not shift
components.a11y: The dot is aria-hidden; the label says the state in words. Non-text marks use tone fg (3:1 or more). The ring is an outline, so it survives forced colors. Use role=status only on a status that changes while the user watches (Test connection), never on every table row. There are no env tones: an environment is not a health state.

components.name: gw-env
components.purpose: Environment marker beside a connection name in every risky context. It differs from a badge by shape: a 2px env-solid bar at the start, square start corners and xs end corners, and an uppercase mono label.
states: display only
components.a11y: Write the slug in lower case in the markup (it is a literal; CSS uppercases it). Where the context does not say 'environment', put environment right before the marker, outside it. Env fg on env subtle is 4.5:1; the env bar is 3:1 on surface and overlay (verified).

components.name: gw-mode
components.purpose: Display-only tool mode, icon plus words: Off (circle-off, neutral), Read only (eye, info), Approval (user-check, warning). To choose a mode, use gw-segmented. There is no write mode.
subparts: direct child .gw-icon (12px, sized by the component)
states: display only
components.a11y: The icon is decorative; the words carry the mode. Tone fg on tone subtle is verified. The transparent border keeps the shape in forced colors.

components.name: gw-tag / gw-tag-list
components.purpose: A value shown as a 24px token: an allowlist entry (host, IP, CIDR, schema), a scope, or an active log-explorer filter, with an optional real remove button. gw-tag-list is the wrapping list container (ul or div, 6px gap).
subparts: optional leading .gw-icon (12px: circle-alert for invalid, lock for locked)
states: __remove :hover wash, :active, :focus-visible ring
__remove [aria-disabled=true] (preferred, stays focusable) or :disabled: the entry is locked by policy, reason nearby
:focus-within on the tag: the label wraps in full (keyboard path to a truncated value) without a height jump for one line
invalid entry: --danger + circle-alert + a field error naming the value
components.a11y: The remove button is a real <button type=button> with aria-label 'Remove <value>', a 24 x 24 target and the standard focus ring; it is never revealed on hover only. The full value of a truncated label is in title (pointer), in the remove button's name (screen reader) and shows on focus-within (keyboard). After removal, move focus to the next remove button or to the input. The full border keeps the shape in forced colors.

components.name: gw-kv
components.purpose: Key-value facts about one object on a native <dl>: connection details, an event's request block, a call's summary strip. Many objects with the same fields belong in a table.
variants: default (two columns, key column at most 40%, dividers)
gw-kv--inline (pairs in a wrapping row, key above value)
subparts: gw-kv__row (div wrapper of one dt + dd)
states: display only
components.a11y: Native dt/dd pairs. Keys are short nouns without colons. An empty value says None or Never, not a dash. Literals use .gw-mono or gw-code and wrap anywhere. Times show relative words plus absolute ISO in <time datetime>. Keys are text.muted, values text.primary (verified pairs).

components.name: gw-stat
components.purpose: KPI tile (Overview, Insights): label, value with unit, a change shown by icon AND words, an optional note or sparkline. A row of tiles is one <dl class=gw-grid>.
variants: data-sentiment=good (success tone) | bad (danger tone) | neutral on __delta
subparts: gw-stat__chart (96 × 32 slot at the END OF THE VALUE ROW, a <dd>, bottom-aligned with the figures; the label spans the full width above, so values in a row of tiles line up)
states: sentiment colours the delta by meaning, independent of direction
components.a11y: The words carry the direction and size of the change; colour only adds the judgement, which is also written in __meta when it matters ('within target'). Icons are aria-hidden. The sparkline SVG has role=img and an aria-label stating the trend. The unit is separated by a space in the markup.

components.name: gw-progress
components.purpose: How far a task has got (plugin upload, core start, setup checklist). The fraction 0..1 is set via style=--gw-progress on the root, which carries role=progressbar.
states: determinate: fraction clamped 0..1, width transition (collapsed globally under reduced motion)
indeterminate: a 40% segment sweeps inside gw-motion; under reduced motion the whole bar pulses its opacity
failed: bar stops where it stopped, --danger, words in the label
inside [data-gw-countdown][data-urgent] (last minute before auto-deny): the markup swaps --warning for --danger; the time is also written as text
components.a11y: role=progressbar with a name (aria-labelledby or aria-label) plus aria-valuemin/max/now (no valuenow when indeterminate), and aria-valuetext for friendlier words. The bar is tone fg on the raised track (verified 3:1 or more). The track hairline is a border-colour inset, not a shadow. Transparent outlines keep track and fill visible in forced colors.

components.name: gw-meter
components.purpose: A measured amount against a limit (rate limit, response size, rows returned). The page decides the level from its thresholds; the fraction is set via style=--gw-meter.
states: warn and critical: the value takes the tone fg, medium weight and a leading icon (triangle-alert, circle-alert)
components.a11y: role=meter, named by aria-labelledby, with aria-valuemin/max/now and an aria-valuetext that includes the judgement ('near the limit'), because the children are presentational. The level never rests on colour alone.

components.name: gw-empty
components.purpose: Empty state: what will appear here plus one action. Covers first run, no results and all clear. Not for errors (use gw-alert--danger).
variants: default (40px tile with 20px icon, h2-size title)
gw-empty--compact (32px tile with 16px icon, h3-size title, small text)
tile tone via gw-icon-tile--<tone> on __icon (success for all clear)
states: none of its own; situations differ by words and icon
components.a11y:
The title is a real heading at the right outline level, or a

when the container already has the heading. The icon is decorative and the tile border survives forced colors. Inherited --gw-tone-* is reset so a toned container never tints the tile. When results empty out after filtering, announce it with role=status on the list.

components.name: gw-field
components.purpose: Wrapper for one labelled control: a visible label above the control, then error, hint and character counter, tied to the control by aria-describedby. As fieldset.gw-field with legend.gw-field__label it groups checkboxes, radios, segmented controls and choice cards.
variants: --inline (label in a left 1/3 column from md, stacked below; everything else goes in __control)
--nested (kit addition: dependent choices indented under their parent choice, role=group + name)
states: control [aria-invalid=true] + __error (circle-alert icon + text)
__counter[data-over] (danger, semibold, the text says how much over)
a hint followed by a counter shares the row; otherwise the hint is full width
fieldset.gw-field + floated legend.gw-field__label (grid row that still names the group)
components.a11y: A real <label for> (or <legend> for groups). Hint and error are referenced by aria-describedby. Required is programmatic (required / aria-required); 'Optional' and 'Required' are words, and an asterisk is aria-hidden with sr-only text. An error is a red border plus an icon plus text, never colour alone.

components.name: gw-input
components.purpose: Native single-line text input on gw-input-base: 32px, bg.field, border.input (3:1), focus ring at offset 0, red border on aria-invalid that stays while hovered.
states: :disabled
[readonly] (sunken, focusable, copyable)
[aria-invalid=true]
:placeholder-shown
:focus-visible ring
components.a11y: Always inside gw-field with a visible label. A placeholder is an example, never the label. Ports and numbers use type=text inputmode=numeric.

components.name: gw-textarea
components.purpose: Native multi-line input on the same base; vertical resize.
variants: --code (mono, no wrapping, tab-size 2: SQL templates, JSON arguments)
--wrap (soft wrap, pre-wrap: prose such as server instructions; with --code, a statement read in full, e.g. a Playground SQL argument)
states: :disabled
[readonly]
[aria-invalid=true]
components.a11y: A counter (gw-field__counter) goes in aria-describedby. For code, add spellcheck=false and autocapitalize=off.

components.name: gw-select
components.purpose: Native <select> on the same base with a stroked chevron painted in currentColor from two gradients, so no raw colours are needed and it follows the disabled colour. Under forced colours the OS arrow is restored.
states: :disabled (chevron repainted)
[aria-invalid=true]
forced-colors: native arrow
components.a11y: Native keyboard, type-ahead and OS picker. More than four options, or options that change often, go here rather than in gw-segmented.

components.name: gw-input-group
components.purpose: One bordered field made of parts: a literal prefix or suffix (https://, ms, rows) and an in-field button (copy, generate, reveal a new value). The group draws the frame, focus ring, invalid edge and disabled look of its gw-input.
states: :has(input:focus-visible) ring on the group
invalid input → danger border (kept on hover)
readonly → sunken fill
disabled → raised fill
__addon[aria-pressed=true] (brand tint, second icon)
__addon[data-copied] (kit.js copy, success colour, second icon)
components.a11y: An icon-only addon needs an aria-label with its object ('Copy base URL'). Its second .gw-icon is the pressed or copied icon. The copy addon uses data-gw-copy or data-gw-copy-from and kit.js announces 'Copied to clipboard'.

components.name: gw-checkbox
components.purpose: Native checkbox with a drawn 16px box. The transparent input covers the whole choice, so box, label and hint form one target at least 24px tall. Use it for values saved with a form, independent options and select all.
variants: no-label (only __input + __control, name on the input): a centred 24×24 target for table selection
states: :checked (brand solid + on-solid check)
:indeterminate (bar; IDL property set from script)
:disabled (raised box, muted label)
[aria-invalid=true] (danger box edge, kept on hover)
:focus-visible (ring on __control)
:hover
components.a11y: Native semantics. When there is a hint, use a div root with label for and aria-describedby, so the hint is not part of the name. No interactive content inside. Marks are drawn with borders so they survive forced colours.

components.name: gw-radio
components.purpose: Native radio with a drawn 16px ring and a 6px dot, for one of 2–5 options that each need a sentence.
states: :checked
:disabled
[aria-invalid=true]
:focus-visible
:hover
components.a11y: Group in fieldset.gw-field with a legend. Arrow keys move and select natively. The dot is a border disc, visible in forced colours.

components.name: gw-switch
components.purpose: A checkbox with role=switch drawn as a 32×18 track with a 14px thumb, for settings that apply immediately with no Save.
states: :checked (brand solid track, thumb moves to the end; travel only under no-preference motion)
:disabled
:disabled:checked (brand border track)
:focus-visible
:hover
components.a11y: role=switch is announced as on / off. Thumb position is the second cue. The track has a transparent outline and the thumb is a border disc, so both show in forced colours. Never put a switch inside a form that has a Save button.

components.name: gw-segmented
components.purpose: Radio group drawn as joined segments, 32px (28px with --sm). The main case is the tool mode Off / Read only / Approval. The checked option is painted in its tone: tone subtle fill, tone fg text and edge, semibold, with its own icon.
variants: data-tone on __option: off (neutral) | read (info) | approval (warning) | brand success warning danger info neutral dev stage prod; none = brand
states: :checked (tone subtle + tone fg text + tone fg edge + semibold, raised above neighbours; transparent inner outline becomes a second ring in forced colours)
:disabled / [aria-disabled=true] (raised fill, disabled text, not-allowed)
:checked:disabled (muted text, border.input edge, keeps weight)
:hover (unchecked, enabled)
:focus-visible (ring above neighbours)
components.a11y: fieldset + sr-only legend naming the object ('Mode for sql_execute'), or role=radiogroup + aria-label. Native Tab and arrow behaviour, no script. The reason for a disabled option is visible text referenced by the group's and the option's aria-describedby. aria-disabled keeps the option in the arrow order but the app must refuse the change. Selection is never colour alone (weight + edge + icon).

components.name: gw-secret
components.purpose: Write-only secret slot of a gw-field. The frame stays 32px in every state, and there is never a show button for a stored value.
variants: data-state=empty (input; a reveal toggle is allowed only here, as an input-group addon with aria-pressed)
data-state=editing (password input + Cancel + Save, no reveal)
data-state=stored (sunken well: lock-keyhole 'Encrypted', 'version 3 · updated 2 days ago', Replace / Rotate)
data-state=reference (sunken well: provider + reference in mono + Test reference)
states: data-state=empty|editing|stored|reference
a narrow well wraps in 28px rows: __meta truncates, __ref wraps inside its row and is never truncated
components.a11y: stored and reference use role=group + aria-labelledby pointing at the field label. Button names carry the object ('Rotate password for dev-db'). Inputs use type=password autocomplete=new-password. Announce 'Password saved, version 4' after Save.

components.name: gw-choice-card
components.purpose: Radio or checkbox drawn as a card, for choices that need an icon and a sentence: connection type, secret source, environment (with gw-env in the title).
states: :checked (2px brand edge + bg.selected tint + filled indicator with check + brand icon)
:focus-visible (ring around the card via :has)
:disabled (raised, muted)
:disabled:checked
[aria-invalid=true] (danger edge, kept on hover)
:hover (enabled, unchecked, valid)
components.a11y: The native input covers the card, so arrow keys move between radio cards. Name it with aria-labelledby (title) and aria-describedby (description) when the card has more than a title. No buttons or links inside. The check mark is border-drawn and survives forced colours.

components.name: gw-search
components.purpose: Search field: a search icon at the start, a clear button once it has a value, and a key hint ('/') while it is empty and not focused.
states: :placeholder-shown (kbd shown, clear hidden)
has value (clear shown)
:focus (kbd hidden)
:disabled (neither clear nor kbd)
inside gw-toolbar__start: 240px basis that grows

aria-keyshortcuts="/" on the input: the ONE kit.js "/" hook focuses it, only when focus is not in an editable field (input, textarea, select, contenteditable), no modifier is pressed and no menu is open; inside an open modal only its own field counts
single-key shortcuts off: <html data-gw-single-keys="off"> (set by input[data-gw-single-keys-toggle], Settings › General, default on, remembered) and the "/" hook does nothing
components.a11y: The input is named with aria-label or an sr-only label. aria-keyshortcuts="/" and the __kbd hint go only on a field the shared kit.js "/" hook serves (WCAG 2.1.4: it never fires while typing in a field and can be turned off); pages write no keydown handler of their own. The clear button is a 24×24 target named 'Clear search'. kbd is aria-hidden. Use <search> or role=search at page level and send result counts to a status region.

components.name: gw-file-drop
components.purpose: Upload zone (PF4J plugin JAR, OpenAPI, kubeconfig): a <label> around a transparent input type=file, so click, keyboard and drop work without script. The app sets data-state.
states: data-state=idle (dashed strong border, neutral tile)
data-state=dragover (solid brand-fg border, bg.selected tint, brand tile)
data-state=uploaded (solid default border, success tile, mono file name)
data-state=error (danger border and hint, danger tile; aria-invalid on the input)
:disabled (raised, muted)
keyboard focus: ring via :has(input:focus-visible)
components.a11y: The label text names the input and the hint describes it. Remove and replace actions go outside the label. Announce upload results in a status region. State changes icon and text as well as colour.

components.name: gw-form
components.purpose: Form layout: fieldset sections with a legend and description. Single column below lg; from lg the description sits on the left third and the rows on the right, except inside a dialog or drawer. Optional sticky action bar.
variants: --sticky-actions (__actions sticks to the bottom of the scrolling main as an overlay bar with 'Unsaved changes' + Discard + Save)
states: sections divided by a subtle rule with 32px on both sides
stacked inside gw-dialog / gw-drawer at any width
components.a11y: One legend per fieldset, or <section aria-labelledby> with a heading in __section-header. On submit, focus the first invalid field. The primary action is type=submit. __note has role=status and is rendered only while the form is dirty.

components.name: gw-tabs
components.purpose: Sibling views of one object on one page (endpoint: Tools & policies / Tokens / AI apps / Settings; connectors: Installed / Templates / MCP servers). --contained switches the view of the same data in a toolbar (Activity: Events / Traces). Not for flow steps (gw-stepper), page navigation (gw-nav) or 2–3 value settings (gw-segmented).
variants: (default) underline tabs, 40px strip on a 1px rule
--contained: segmented-style tabs in a bordered raised container, 32px overall (26px tabs), hugs its content
subparts: __count (gw-counter metrics: 18px pill, tabular, bg.active; brand tint when its tab is selected; sr-only words)
states: [aria-selected=true]: 2px brand-fg bottom border + primary text + semibold (contained: overlay pill + border-strong + shadow-sm + semibold)
:hover: primary text + border-strong bar hint (contained: bg.hover)
:disabled (kit.js skips it); [aria-disabled=true] styled for parity
:focus-visible: inset ring
panel [hidden]
components.a11y: role=tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-controls ↔ aria-labelledby, tablist named after its object. kit.js: ←/→ Home End with automatic activation, roving tabindex, skips native disabled tabs. Counts carry sr-only words ('14 tools'). Selection has three cues (bar, weight, text colour); the bar is a border so it survives forced colours.

components.name: gw-menu-host / gw-menu / gw-popover
components.purpose: The kit's only dropdown. role=menu holds actions on one object; role=listbox picks one value with a check (sort, time range); gw-popover (role=dialog) holds a small form next to its trigger (add filter, columns, appearance). Opens on click / Enter / Space only.
variants: gw-menu--right (align to the trigger's end edge)
gw-popover--right (align to the trigger's end edge)
gw-menu--up (opens above the trigger; state class set by kit.js when there is more room above)
gw-menu__item--active / [data-active] (the option an aria-activedescendant listbox points at: hover wash + inset ring; command palette)
subparts: gw-menu-host (position: relative; trigger must be its direct child)
gw-menu: __group __item __icon __label __hint (block inside __label, or truncating inline value at row end) __check __kbd __divider __note
states: [hidden] closed
:hover / :focus-visible: bg.hover wash + inset ring; hint and kbd lift to text.secondary (danger: danger.subtle wash)
:disabled / [aria-disabled=true]: disabled text, no wash
[aria-selected=true] / [aria-checked=true] shows __check (the space is kept otherwise)
trigger [aria-expanded=true]
__item--active / [data-active] (aria-activedescendant listboxes)

open: TOP LAYER (popover="manual" + showPopover()), position: fixed from the trigger's rect, at least 4px from the viewport edge, flipped --up when there is more room above, follows scrolling and resizing; a gw-table-wrap or a dialog body never clips it
no Popover API: the panel stays absolute inside its host (--up still flips it)
components.a11y: Trigger: <button aria-haspopup=menu|listbox|dialog aria-expanded aria-controls> as a direct child of .gw-menu-host. Items tabindex=-1; kit.js handles arrows, Home / End, Esc (returns focus), and closes on Tab / outside click; one panel open at a time; option / menuitemradio update aria-selected / aria-checked and [data-gw-menu-value]. Popover: role=dialog + aria-labelledby → __title; focus goes to the first field and leaving closes it. __kbd is aria-hidden (aria-keyshortcuts only for real shortcuts); group headings are __note aria-hidden referenced by role=group aria-labelledby. z --gw-z-popover, overlay surface, entry drop only inside gw-motion.

components.name: gw-tooltip
components.purpose: CSS-only short hint next to its trigger: the name of an icon-only button, the absolute time behind a relative one, why a control is unavailable. Never interactive content (use gw-popover).
variants: --end (aligned to the trigger's end edge); side and alignment compose
subparts: __bubble (role=tooltip; bg.inverse / text.inverse, caption type, radius sm, max 280px, transparent border for forced colours)
states: shown on .gw-tooltip:hover (after duration-base) and :has(:focus-visible) (at once)
stays while the pointer moves onto the bubble (gap bridge)
hidden while the wrapped trigger has [aria-expanded=true]
plain-text trigger child with tabindex=0: dotted underline + focus ring
components.a11y: aria-labelledby → bubble when it is the name, aria-describedby when it adds information. Hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13). Use aria-disabled (not disabled) so keyboard users reach the reason. Esc-to-dismiss is not provided by kit.js (gap). RTL-safe centring.

components.name: gw-dialog / gw-drawer
components.purpose: Native <dialog> opened with showModal(). gw-dialog is centred and holds one question or one short task (revoke a token, create an endpoint). gw-drawer is pinned to the inline-end edge at full height, for reading beside the list (event detail, trace).
variants: gw-dialog--danger (irreversible actions AND untrusted code: unsigned plugin install, external MCP server review; header icon tile in the danger tone; confirm is gw-btn--danger and names the object; Cancel has autofocus)
gw-drawer--md (560, default) / --lg (720), never wider than the viewport

gw-dialog--warning (risky but reversible confirm: publish the tunnel, change the port, accept calls from any address; amber icon tile; the confirm is a normal or primary button, never --danger; Cancel has autofocus; an Undo toast never brings the exposure back)
subparts: __header (grid: [gw-icon-tile] title + description [close]; drawer: fixed bar with a bottom rule)
__close (gw-btn ghost icon sm, aria-label Close, data-gw-dialog-close)
__body (the only scroller; 4px top room for focus rings)
__footer (end-aligned actions: secondary first, primary / danger last)
states: [open] (native; closed = UA display: none)
::backdrop = bg.backdrop
data-gw-static: backdrop click does not close (forms with input)
components.a11y: Focus trap, Esc, inert page and focus return come from showModal(). aria-labelledby → title, aria-describedby → description. EVERY gw-dialog names its initial focus in the markup: autofocus on the first field (or the first control when there are no fields), or on Cancel in a confirmation (Deny in the OAuth sign-in consent). Motion: the dialog fades, rises and scales; the drawer slides from the inline-end edge (RTL-aware). Reduced motion: fade only.

components.name: gw-toast-region / gw-toast
components.purpose: Short-lived feedback in the bottom-end corner: the result of an action (Token revoked, with Undo), or an event that needs no answer now. Never the only place a decision or an error lives.
subparts: gw-toast-region (fixed bottom-end, z --gw-z-toast, width --gw-layout-toast-width, max viewport − 32px, clicks pass through gaps)
states: enter: fade; rise inside gw-motion
auto-dismiss after 6 s (kit.js; timeout: 0 keeps it)
components.a11y: Region <section aria-label="Notifications"> (kit.js creates one if missing and appends to the first one). Toasts are role=status, role=alert only for danger. Tone is backed by an icon and words. Do not auto-dismiss a toast whose actions the user must reach.

components.name: gw-alert
components.purpose: A message about a state that holds while it is true: inline in a section or form, as a --banner above the page for app-wide state (Core stopped, Tunnel is public), or --compact on one line in a card, row or form. Says what happened and what to do.
variants: --banner (full width, no radius, bottom rule only, page-gutter padding; actions move under the text below sm)
--compact (one line, 32px min, title and body inline and wrapping; link actions get a 24px target)
subparts: __actions (inside __content: under the text; a direct child: at the end of the row)
states: none (display only); role=status / role=alert once when it appears in response to something
components.a11y: Tone subtle fill + tone border + tone icon; text stays primary / secondary (passes 4.5:1 on every subtle fill in all four themes). Never colour alone: icon + title words. A static alert has no role.

components.name: gw-stepper
components.purpose: Position in a short linear flow of 3–5 steps (Add connection: Choose type, Configure, Test, Add to endpoint; onboarding). Shows progress; not navigation, not tabs, not a checklist. --guide is the short first-run guide whose steps lead to the pages where the work is done.
variants: (default) horizontal from md (960px) with connectors filling the row, vertical below md
--guide (first-run guide on Overview: always vertical, the label is an h3, __content holds the step's actions; actions of an upcoming step are aria-disabled with a reason)
states: data-state=complete: brand solid marker + check icon, brand connector after it, sr-only ', completed'
data-state=current: 2px brand ring + brand-subtle fill + brand number + semibold label, aria-current=step
data-state=upcoming: border-strong ring + muted number + secondary label
data-state=error: 2px danger ring + danger-subtle fill + x icon, danger description, sr-only ', failed', aria-current=step
components.a11y: <ol aria-label="<flow name>">; markers are decorative; complete / failed are spoken through sr-only text and current through aria-current=step; never colour alone (icon, ring, weight). --guide: the label is a heading one level below the enclosing heading (h3 under a card h2); an upcoming step's actions are aria-disabled + aria-describedby → a visible reason.

components.name: gw-paginator
components.purpose: Moving through long lists. Compact: range + prev / next under server-sorted tables. Numbered: page buttons for short browsable lists (connector catalog). Load older: a cursor button for the audit log (never page numbers).
variants: compact (__info + gw-btn ghost icon sm prev / next)
numbered (ul.__controls of __page buttons, aria-current=page, ellipsis gap)
load older (gw-btn sm, aria-busy + gw-spinner while loading, end-of-log text)
subparts: __page (gw-pressable sm, 28px; <span> = gap marker inside an aria-hidden li)
states: __page[aria-current=page]: bg.selected + brand border + brand text + semibold
:hover wash, :focus-visible ring
:disabled prev / next at the ends
[aria-busy=true] on Load older
components.a11y: <nav aria-label="… pages"> when it navigates; page buttons are named 'Page 3' and prev / next 'Previous page' / 'Next page'; announce the new range with window.gwAnnounce after a change; targets ≥ 28px.

components.name: gw-skeleton
components.purpose: Placeholder in the shape of content that is about to arrive (first render of a list, card, chart or table when the wait passes about 300 ms). Not for in-place actions (spinner), long jobs (gw-progress) or failures (gw-alert--danger).
variants: --text (12px bar in a 20px line box; the last of several lines is 64%)
states: calm opacity pulse 1.6 s; with reduced motion 3.2 s, opacity only, never a shimmer
components.a11y: Blocks (or their row / wrapper) are aria-hidden. The loading region carries aria-busy=true plus an sr-only role=status naming what loads; remove both when content arrives. Fill bg.active reads on surface, raised and canvas in every theme.

components.name: gw-code / gw-code-block / gw-tok-*
components.purpose: Literals shown verbatim in mono with ligatures off. gw-code is an inline chip for one literal (tool name, slug, host, path, token prefix). gw-code-block is a multi-line block for SQL, commands, JSON, TOML and command output, with copy via data-gw-copy-from. gw-tok-* are the syntax token colours from --gw-color-code-*.
variants: gw-code--secret (masked placeholder ‹masked›: secret colour, dashed edge; the guillemets are the non-colour cue)
gw-code-block--numbered (CSS-counter line-number gutter, sticky on horizontal scroll, not copied, not read aloud; --gw-code-gutter: 4ch for 1000+ lines)

gw-tok-invisible (a visible escape such as ‹U+202E›, ‹U+200B›, ‹TAB›, ‹SP› written INSTEAD of an invisible, bidi, zero-width or control character, a tab or a trailing space; dashed frame + bold, code point and name in title; required in approval requests)
gw-tok-confusable (a real non-ASCII look-alike letter outside a string literal, such as U+043E in an identifier; framed, with the code point in title)
subparts: gw-code-block__actions (end, ghost sm button 4px from the edge)
states: [data-copied] on the copy button (kit.js, 1.6 s) swaps __copy for __copied
__body:focus-visible (inset ring)
components.a11y: __body is a keyboard-scrollable region: tabindex=0 + role=region + aria-label. The copy button has visible text plus a gw-sr-only object ('Copy SQL query'). The copied face changes the accessible name to 'Copied', and kit.js announces it. Line numbers use content: counter() / "", so they are neither read nor copied. With line spans present, the line container becomes a grid, so the copy stays exact. Every token colour is 4.5:1 or more on code.bg in all four modes.

components.name: gw-diff
components.purpose: Unified diff of the exact change a human confirms: what Connect writes into a client config (~/.codex/config.toml), what k8s_apply changes in a manifest.
variants: gw-diff--wrap (soft-wraps long lines instead of scrolling sideways; a wrapped line hangs 2ch under its text, gutters and marker stay on the first line; always on inside approval-request)
states: __body:focus-visible (inset ring)
components.a11y: The + and − (U+2212) markers are text, so the change survives greyscale, high contrast and forced colours. Markers and gutters are aria-hidden; each changed line carries a gw-sr-only prefix ('Added: ' / 'Removed: ') that is excluded from text selection. __body is a named, focusable scroll region. All rows share one subgrid, so gutters line up and washes span the full width. Gutter and marker use diff fg on their wash (4.5:1); line text stays code.text.

components.name: gw-copy-field
components.purpose: Read-only value plus a Copy button: endpoint URL, CLI command, and a token at the one moment it is visible.
variants: gw-copy-field--secret-once (warning frame; the <code> value wraps and stays fully visible; __hint 'Shown once. Store it in your password manager.')
subparts: gw-copy-field__value (<code>, or <input readonly> inside a gw-field)
states: [data-copied] on __button swaps the faces (kit.js)
focus ring on the whole field while an <input> value is :focus-visible
components.a11y: Name the field: role=group + aria-labelledby around a <code> value, or <label for> on an <input readonly> value (focusable; Ctrl+A selects it). The button text includes a gw-sr-only object ('Copy endpoint URL'). In --secret-once the button's aria-describedby points to the hint. The field is 36px tall: a 28px button inset by 4px.

components.name: gw-table-wrap / gw-table
components.purpose: Native <table> for dense, sortable lists of objects with the same fields (Activity calls, connections, tokens, secrets). The wrap is the framed scroller.
variants: gw-table--interactive (each row has a __row-link; pointer over the row)
gw-table--sticky (sticky thead inside a wrap with --gw-table-max-height)
gw-table__cell--optional (a secondary column: Type, Credentials, Version, AI app, Duration; hidden below lg; on the th AND every td; never the row key, a status or the actions)

gw-table__cell--sticky-end (the action cell of a full-width alert row, e.g. Test again of an unreachable billing-api: pinned to the end edge while the wrap scrolls, keeps the row's hover / selected fill)
states: th[aria-sort=none|ascending|descending] shows the matching icon; a sorted header turns primary (kit.js cycles and announces)
tr[aria-selected=true]: selected fill + 2px brand bar (kit.js mirrors data-gw-select-row / data-gw-select-all)
row-link :focus-visible: ring drawn on the row
__sort and wrap :focus-visible
inside gw-card--flush: frameless, card inner corners, inset ring
gw-table-wrap scroll shadows: an edge with more columns behind it shows a soft shade on that side (pure CSS, no script)
Activity events: Time | Decision | Tool · connection (stacked) | AI app · endpoint (stacked) | Duration; extra columns only with __cell--optional; never scrolls sideways at 1440 × 900
components.a11y: A real table with <caption> (gw-sr-only when a heading names it); the wrap is role=region + aria-labelledby (the caption) + tabindex=0. Sorting uses a button inside th[aria-sort]. Row checkboxes have aria-labels that name the row, and the checkbox carries the selection state. The row link's text plus a gw-sr-only phrase names the row. Row actions are always visible, sit above the stretched link and have targets of 24px or more. A hidden data table (the numbers behind a chart) is not a gw-table: a plain <table> inside <div class="gw-sr-only">.

components.name: gw-chart / gw-legend / gw-sparkline
components.purpose: Library-free charts in HTML, CSS and SVG: a stacked histogram of calls over time by decision, a horizontal bar list (top tools, share of a whole) and a sparkline. Data enters as unitless --v custom properties.
states: __bar[aria-pressed=true] (interactive): selected fill + 2px brand bar on top
__bar:focus-visible ring, hover wash
components.a11y: The chart root is role=img with an aria-label stating the finding, and the same numbers sit beside it in a <table> with a caption inside <div class="gw-sr-only"> (the class goes on the wrapper, never on the table). In the interactive histogram the root is role=group and each bar button's aria-label carries its numbers. Series differ by legend words, fixed stack order and 1px gaps, not colour alone. Marks paint with tone fg or chart tokens (3:1 or more), never solids, and keep their fills in forced colours. The sparkline is aria-hidden next to a number, otherwise role=img + aria-label.

components.name: gw-waterfall
components.purpose: Where one call's time went (event-detail Timing): gateway work vs time in the resource vs the idle wait for a human decision.
components.a11y: An <ol> named by aria-label or aria-labelledby (tool, connection, total). Tracks are aria-hidden: each row reads 'phase, duration'. Spans are placed with --start/--len (0..1) and are never thinner than 2px. The approval wait is hatched, which says 'idle' without colour; the legend uses gw-legend__swatch--hatch for it. Rows share a subgrid, and labels truncate at narrow widths.

components.name: gw-timeline
components.purpose: Vertical feed of what happened, in order: the approval path (requested → notified → approved → executed), the steps of an agent trace.
variants: empty marker renders a dot (dense trace steps)
states: li[aria-current=step]: marker filled with the tone solid (icon in on-solid) + semibold title
components.a11y: An <ol> with an aria-label. The title says what happened in words; the tone and icon (aria-hidden) are extra cues. Times are <time datetime> with the full ISO time in title. The current step is shown by fill plus weight, not colour alone, and the comment corner radii are logical, so RTL is correct.

elements.name: setup-map
elements.purpose: Light visualisation of what to configure and how it connects, in SETUP order: Secrets & resources → Connections (where tools run; the secret is injected here, and a side note says so) → Policies (decides each call: mode, limits, approval) → Endpoints (one MCP URL, token or OAuth) → AI apps, left to right (top to bottom when stacked), matching getting-started and the onboarding stepper. A caption under the map (aria-hidden) and the list's aria-describedby sentence say: "Set it up left to right. An agent's call travels the other way: AI app → endpoint → policy → connection, where the secret is injected." Each node shows its icon tile, title, what it does, a one-line status with counts (a todo status says what it waits for or 'start here'), a state badge (done / attention / todo) and a Configure link to its page. Decorative arrows join the nodes and take their state from the two nodes they connect. The --wiring variant for endpoint-detail is unchanged: the AI apps that call the endpoint (client marks + status) → the endpoint (URL copy field, sign-in badges, mode summary '6 read only · 3 approval · 5 off', policy) → its connections (type tile, name + env marker, health).
states: step data-state=done: gw-badge--success circle-check 'Done', tile --brand
step data-state=attention: gw-badge--warning triangle-alert 'Needs attention', tile --warning; the status names the problem ('billing-api unreachable')
step data-state=todo: gw-badge--neutral circle-dashed 'Not set up', tile --neutral, gw-card--dashed; the status says what it waits for ('needs a connection first') or 'start here'
connector done→done: brand-fg solid; a todo on either side: border-strong dashed; otherwise: border-strong solid; arrows centred between the cards
layout: compact vertical below md, one row per node md–lg, horizontal chain from lg (equal columns, arrows in the gap, the note in a shared second row)
--vertical: always stacked with compact nodes, for narrow columns
--wiring: AI apps → endpoint → Connections (endpoint-detail); names truncate with title, the status column is capped at 128px and wraps
demo: all set up, first run (only the master key done), needs attention (billing-api unreachable, Cursor needs restart), wiring, narrow column
setup order: Secrets & resources → Connections → Policies → Endpoints → AI apps; 'start here' sits on the first todo node (usually Secrets & resources)
caption + aria-describedby: 'Set it up left to right. An agent's call travels the other way: AI app → endpoint → policy → connection, where the secret is injected.'

elements.name: how-it-works
elements.purpose: Compact, collapsible strip of 3–4 numbered steps that explains a mechanism before the user configures it: what happens to a secret, how an AI app is authorized, what one-click Connect writes, three ways to extend connectors. Each step has a number (gw-counter, aria-hidden; the <ol> gives the position), an icon tile, a short bold title and one line of explanation. An optional Learn more link sits under the steps. The header keeps the title and a one-line summary visible when the strip is collapsed; the disclosure is a ghost icon button with data-gw-toggle, aria-expanded and aria-controls.
states: expanded: button aria-expanded=true, panel visible, chevron-up
collapsed: aria-expanded=false + hidden on the panel, chevron-down; the title and summary stay
layout: a list below lg (the title line centred on the tile); from lg a strip of 3 or 4 equal columns with a muted chevron centred in the gap, level with the tiles
--vertical: always a list, for the settings column
demo: Secrets (4 steps, expanded, Learn more), Connectors (3 steps, no Learn more), Authorization (--vertical), AI apps (collapsed)

elements.name: getting-started
elements.purpose: First-run checklist card with a progress summary ('5 of 6 done' + gw-progress) and six ordered steps: Protect your master key, Add a connection, Create an endpoint, Connect your AI app, Try a tool in Playground, Set up approval notifications. Each step has a status icon, a title, one line on why it matters and one action. Only the current step gets the primary button; the others are links, so steps can be done out of order. Done steps fold to one line with what was done. A ghost button dismisses the checklist; that can be undone, so the app shows a toast with Undo. When all steps are done the card becomes a calm summary with the steps behind a disclosure.
states: step data-state=done: circle-check in a gw-fg-success __icon span; one line of title + meta; sr-only ', done'
step data-state=current: circle-dot in gw-fg-brand; semibold title; aria-current=step; the only gw-btn--primary
step data-state=todo: circle-dashed in gw-fg-muted; gw-btn--link action; sr-only ', not done yet'
fresh install (0 of 6, step 1 current)
in progress (5 of 6, the demo world as on Overview: done rows folded, Try a tool in Playground current while the later notifications step is already done)
complete (gw-getting-started--complete: success tile summary, steps behind a data-gw-toggle disclosure, no progress bar, no confetti)
dismissed (card removed; toast with Undo in the app)
action / meta column capped at 256px; below sm the action drops under the text

elements.name: approval-request
elements.purpose: The decision UI for one mutation an agent asked for. It shows the exact action verbatim (gw-code-block for SQL, command or HTTP; gw-diff for k8s_apply; always wrapped, invisible characters as gw-tok-invisible escapes, look-alike letters as gw-tok-confusable), with the connection and its gw-env (__target keeps them on one line), endpoint, AI app and token, and a countdown to auto-deny. Below that: why approval is needed (the policy rule in words plus its id) and the impact, then the agent's note marked unverified. Pending requests end with a comment (optional on dev and stage, REQUIRED on prod by default) and Deny / Approve and run. After a decision the footer is a read-only history (gw-timeline). The --compact row for lists has Review only, never Approve. On the desktop there is one approver, you ('by you'); multi-approver partial is a server-mode state. Through the protocol (MCP 2026-07-28 input_required) a client gets the request id, the verbatim action (read-only) and a link to approvals.html#ap-<id>, never a field it could fill to approve.
states: data-state=pending (default): badge warning hourglass 'Waiting for approval', countdown 'Auto-deny in 4:12' (data-gw-countdown + data-gw-countdown-text, gw-progress--sm --warning fed by --gw-countdown), decision group: comment, Deny (--danger), Approve and run (--approve, last)
pending, urgent: kit.js sets [data-urgent] at 60 s or less; the markup swaps gw-progress--warning for --danger and puts gw-fg-danger on the whole timer line; the app announces once via role=alert

prod: gw-env--prod in the title plus a gw-alert--danger 'This runs on production' first in the body; comment required (below); prod window 10 min; prod connections only through incident-prod, prod-vm only through runbooks
data-state=approved: badge success user-check 'Approved'; the footer is the history, current step (aria-current=step) is the run
data-state=rejected: badge danger user-x 'Rejected'; history with the approver's comment (the contract's 'denied': a human Deny is recorded as Rejected; policy denials never create a request)
data-state=expired: badge neutral timer-off 'Expired', gw-alert--neutral --compact 'Nothing ran', history; read-only
data-state=executed: badge 'Approved' plus gw-alert--success 'Executed in 38 ms', '1 row affected', View event, history

pages.title: Core starting · GateRook
pages.purpose: The window shown while the gateway core is unavailable. It uses no gw-shell and no data-gw-nav: the status-screen element is the page's <main>. The live state is Unlock required: a neutral lock tile, an explanation of OS protection and the possible system prompt, the legacy macOS Safe Storage entry name, and Quit + Unlock GateRook. The demo also covers waiting for the operating system with a busy button. The explanation says that denying access closes GateRook. Denial or cancellation closes the app without starting the core. No password field or metadata line is shown, and the core starts only after successful unlock. Starting ('Starting the native core and the local API … about a second'): an indeterminate progress bar and vertical steps Native core done ('Native image · 0.1 s'), Master key done, Database migrations done, Local API on 127.0.0.1:7465 in progress, plus an sr-only status line. A small keyboard-accessible demo switcher at the bottom (gw-tabs--contained, arrows/Home/End) shows the other documented states. Port in use: the failed Local API step, an open 'Find the process' panel with lsof plus a Windows netstat line, then Quit and 'Use another port', which opens a warning dialog listing what changes (candidate 7475, since 7466 is the tunnel's public listener; clients with the URL in their config connect again; Claude Desktop's bridge asks the app for the new URL; a claude.ai row only for a named tunnel or an ngrok domain). Master key not found: the Master key step failed while Database migrations and Local API are done (the locked core has migrated and listens); a danger alert (the 8 secrets encrypted here become unreadable; the 3 references keep working; 11 in all, as in Secrets) with a danger-ghost 'Create a new key' that opens a danger dialog with the consequences and Cancel autofocused; Quit and 'Restore from backup' as the primary, which opens a dialog modelled on Back up master key (an optional passphrase, autofocused, then the system open dialog: 'Choose the backup file'). Stopped: exit facts in gw-kv, the last log lines collapsed, the 3 pending approvals kept, Open logs and 'Restart core'. Didn't start: any other ready:false reason, here DB_LOCKED ('Another core is using the database'), with the stopped card's facts, Open logs and 'Restart core'. A tiny script keeps <main> data-state and aria-labelledby in sync with the shown card.
